answer: Stop sybils with a quill that writes in its owner's pigment. Each identity must keep a memory-hard sequential proof tied to its own history: sequential, so a farm cannot parallelize it, and memory-hard, so one machine cannot hold many proofs at once — N clones need N machines and N sequential waits. Each proof is dyed with a pigment of its owner's past actions, so a copied proof stains every clone that reuses it. The protocol also plants a fable as a canary: a decoy invitation only a shared operator would answer twice alike, and any identity that bites loses its bond plus its sponsors' bonds.
